title: School and work
goal: Name jobs and school levels, talk around the office, and use polite sentences with your boss or teacher.
bekal: addressing your boss, teachers and elders at the right level

dialogs.title: Paguneman — At the office
dialogs.intro: It's Rani's first day at the Bandung branch office. Pak Dadang, the head of department, shows her around and introduces her to the team.

lines.speaker: Pa Dadang:
lines.text: Wilujeng énjing, Néng Rani. Kumaha, tos betah?
lines.id: Good morning, Rani. So, settling in?
lines.literal: good morning, Néng Rani. how, already at-home?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Wilujeng énjing, Pa. Alhamdulillah tos rada betah.
lines.id: Good morning, sir. Thank God, I'm starting to feel at home.
lines.literal: good morning, Pa. alhamdulillah already somewhat at-home.

lines.speaker: Pa Dadang:
lines.text: Saé. Ieu tim urang. Kang Yayan, Téh Nia, sareng Mang Ohim.
lines.id: Good. This is our team: Kang Yayan, Téh Nia and Mang Ohim.
lines.literal: good. this team we. Kang Yayan, Téh Nia, and Mang Ohim.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Wilujeng patepang sadayana. Nami abdi Rani.
lines.id: Nice to meet you all. My name is Rani.
lines.literal: safe meeting all. name my Rani.

lines.speaker: Kang Yayan:
lines.text: Wilujeng sumping, Téh. Ti Jakarta nya?

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Muhun. Punten upami basa Sunda abdi masih kaku.
lines.id: Yes. Sorry if my Sundanese is still a bit stiff.
lines.literal: yes. excuse-me if language Sundanese my still stiff.

lines.speaker: Téh Nia:
lines.text: Teu nanaon. Urang mah sok maké basa Indonesia ogé di kantor.
lines.id: No problem. We often use Indonesian at the office too.
lines.literal: no what-what. we [mah] like use language Indonesian also at office.

lines.speaker: Pa Dadang:
lines.text: Tapi diajar mah alus. Sing daék naros ka Kang Yayan.
lines.id: But learning is great. Don't be shy about asking Kang Yayan.
lines.literal: but study [mah] good. may willing ask to Kang Yayan.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Muhun, Pa. Damelan abdi dinten ieu naon?
lines.id: Yes, sir. What's my work for today?
lines.literal: yes, Pa. work my day this what?

lines.speaker: Pa Dadang:
lines.text: Dinten ieu mah maca laporan heula. Énjing kakara rapat.
lines.id: Today, read the reports first. The meeting is tomorrow.
lines.literal: day this [mah] read report first. tomorrow only meeting.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: What time is the meeting, sir?

lines.speaker: Pa Dadang:
lines.text: Tabuh salapan énjing. Ulah telat nya, di dieu mah ketat.
lines.id: Nine in the morning. Don't be late, they're strict here.
lines.literal: hour nine morning. don't late [nya], at here [mah] strict.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Siap, Pa. Hatur nuhun tos dibimbing.
lines.id: Yes, sir. Thank you for showing me the ropes.
lines.literal: ready, Pa. thank you already guided.

notes: **Wilujeng patepang** = nice to meet you, literally "safe meeting." It's the best phrase for introductions, and more Sundanese than the borrowed Indonesian *salam kenal*.
**Damelan** = work, task (lemes); loma: **pagawéan**. Both come from the verbs *damel*/*gawé* (to work).
**Kaku** = stiff, also used for a language you don't speak fluently yet. *Punten upami basa Sunda abdi masih kaku* is a very handy sentence: it asks for understanding before any mistake happens.
**Sing daék** = "may you be willing," used as gentle encouragement. **Sing** makes a wish: *sing betah* (hope you settle in), *sing damang* (stay healthy), *sing lancar* (hope it goes smoothly).
**Ketat** (strict) and many other office words are borrowed straight from Indonesian. That's normal: office talk in Bandung is mixed, and nobody expects pure Sundanese in a meeting room.

grammars.title: Speaking to your boss and teachers
body: At work and at school, the speech level depends on position, not age. A boss younger than you still gets lemes.
after: ⚠️ Calling colleagues your age **Kang** (for men) or **Téh** (for women) is a Bandung office habit worth following from day one. A bare name with no title feels cold, though it isn't wrong.

The sentences you'll need most with your boss: **Punten, badé naros sakedik** (excuse me, may I ask something), **Tos rengse, Pa** (it's done, sir), **Hapunten, abdi teu acan ngartos** (sorry, I don't understand yet), **Kenging widi teu?** (may I have permission?).
Reporting on your work: **nuju dikerjakeun** (in progress), **tos rengse** (done), **teu acan rengse** (not finished yet), **kedah dirévisi** (needs revising).

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Tukang** means "the person who does it, the expert" and is very productive: *tukang bakso* (meatball-soup seller), *tukang beca* (pedicab driver), *tukang cukur* (barber), *tukang kebon* (gardener). The same word also means "back, behind." Context tells them apart, and you met both in Unit 11.

sections.title: At the office and in class

blocks.title: At the office
items: **Punten, badé naros sakedik.** — Excuse me, may I ask something?
**Tos rengse, Pa.** — It's done, sir.
**Nuju dikerjakeun.** — It's in progress.
**Kenging widi teu, badé ka luar sakedap?** — May I step out for a moment?
**Hapunten abdi telat, macét pisan.** — Sorry I'm late, the traffic was terrible.
**Rapatna dimimitian tabuh sabaraha?** — What time does the meeting start?
**Punten, tiasa dibantosan?** — Excuse me, could you help?
**Abdi badé wangsul heula, Pa.** — I'll head home first, sir.

blocks.title: In class
items: **Punten, Bu Guru, abdi teu acan ngartos.** — Excuse me, ma'am, I don't understand yet.
**Tiasa diterangkeun deui?** — Could you explain it again?
**Punten, kumaha nyebatna dina basa Sunda?** — Excuse me, how do you say it in Sundanese?
**Naon hartosna kecap ieu?** — What does this word mean?
**Punten, PR-na kanggo iraha?** — Excuse me, when is the homework due?
**Hatur nuhun tos diwulang.** — Thank you for teaching us.

blocks.text: **Ngawulang** = to teach (lemes); loma: **ngajar**. The passive is *diwulang* = to be taught. The closing line *hatur nuhun tos diwulang* is what pupils traditionally say to their teacher in West Java, and it's always warmly received.

items: someone who teaches at a school → ____
someone who works in the rice fields → ____
someone who sells things → ____
someone who drives an angkot → ____
someone who performs wayang golek puppet shows → ____
